name: Ironclad Agrisystems Particulate Veil Dispersal Unit
product_name: Ironclad Agrisystems Particulate Veil Dispersal Unit
description:
The Particulate Veil Dispersal Unit is a backpack-mounted aerosol system originally designed by Ironclad Agrisystems for precision micro-particle application in enclosed agricultural environments — specifically, the dispersion of reflective particulate coatings over hydroponic grow surfaces to optimize light distribution. Operatives in GLMZ's underground quickly recognized that the same micro-particle chemistry, when dispersed in quantity, creates a dense aerosol cloud that simultaneously scatters laser-based motion detection grids, diffuses millimeter-wave scanning beams, and reduces optical camera resolution to near-zero within the cloud boundary.

The unit carries two interchangeable canister types: the standard agricultural reflective particulate (which creates a brilliant white-out cloud visible to the naked eye but highly effective against sensor systems) and the tactical low-visibility variant developed by third-party chemical suppliers for the gray market, which uses near-IR-transparent particles that are nearly invisible in normal lighting while retaining sensor-scattering properties. Dispersal duration and cloud density are controlled via a wrist-mounted dial, and the unit can sustain a moving cloud around a small team for approximately twelve minutes per canister at medium dispersal rates.

Ironclad Agrisystems has never officially acknowledged the tactical applications of the Dispersal Unit and continues to market it as an agricultural tool. The company has resisted regulatory pressure to restrict sales, citing the agricultural sector's reliance on the product and pointing out, accurately, that the base unit is not modified in any way for the tactical canisters — those are sourced entirely through third parties. This legal distance has kept the base unit in an unrestricted commercial category while the tactical canisters occupy a much grayer legal space.
legality: Unrestricted (base unit and agricultural canisters); Restricted (tactical low-visibility canisters)

specifications.dispersal_range: Up to 8 meters forward arc (medium rate), 4 meters (low rate)
specifications.canister_types: Agricultural reflective (standard, unrestricted); Tactical near-IR-transparent (gray market, restricted)
specifications.laser_grid_disruption: Effective against standard 650 nm and 780 nm motion detection lasers
specifications.mmwave_disruption: ~71% signal degradation at 24–77 GHz within cloud boundary
specifications.optical_camera_disruption: Near-zero resolution within cloud (agricultural canister); Partial disruption (tactical canister)
specifications.backpack_form_factor: Low-profile agricultural worker harness, concealable under a work coat

tactical_use: Deployed during approach and breach phases in sensor-heavy environments. The agricultural canister is used when visual detection by human guards is less of a concern than sensor defeat — the white-out cloud is extremely effective but obvious. Tactical canisters are used in environments with both sensor systems and human or camera observation. Teams typically move through the dispersal cloud in tight formation, using the 8-meter forward arc to clear sensor coverage ahead of them. The unit's agricultural worker aesthetic makes it surprisingly effective for social infiltration in industrial and logistics zones where such equipment is commonplace.
cultural_context: The Particulate Veil Dispersal Unit has an unusual cultural footprint in GLMZ — it is simultaneously a genuine piece of working agricultural equipment used by thousands of hydroponic facility workers and one of the most common sensor-defeat tools in the city's infiltration community. This dual identity gives it a kind of operational camouflage that purpose-built tactical gear lacks: a person carrying a Dispersal Unit on their back in an industrial district is almost certainly a maintenance worker, until suddenly they're not. Among operatives, the unit is considered a 'working class' piece of kit — unpretentious, effective, and available at any agri-supply depot. The tactical canisters are the tell that separates the professionals from the opportunists.
known_users: Mid-tier infiltration teams operating in industrial zones
Protest groups and civil disruption networks (agricultural canisters used against security drones)
Smuggling operations running goods through sensor-monitored logistics corridors
Ironclad Agrisystems field technicians (unaware of secondary market)
story_hooks: A rash of sensor-grid defeats across a corporate logistics district is traced to Dispersal Units — but the tactical canisters being used contain a novel particulate formulation that no known gray-market supplier produces, suggesting someone has developed a proprietary upgrade and is distributing it through the underground.

Ironclad Agrisystems receives pressure from a major corporate client to add a tracking chip to all Dispersal Units sold in GLMZ, ostensibly for 'agricultural inventory management.' A whistleblower contacts the players for help stopping the rollout before it burns dozens of active operators.

A player's team uses a Dispersal Unit during an infiltration, only to find that the sensor-scattering cloud has inadvertently triggered a chemical alarm in the facility — the particulates are interacting with something in the building's HVAC system, and now they're locked in with a full security response and a slowly thickening toxic atmosphere.

The gray-market supplier of tactical canisters in the players' district has gone dark. Investigation reveals they were acquired by an unknown corporate entity — and the last batch of tactical canisters they distributed has been quietly reformulated to include a biomarker that tags anyone who enters the dispersal cloud for later identification.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, utilitarian backpack-mounted aerosol dispersal system disguised as agricultural equipment. Twin cylindrical pressure vessels dominate the rear, flanked by a dense network of microfluidic distribution tubing and brass check valves. The dispersal nozzle is a wide, flared trumpet resembling a crop-duster attachment. Overall impression is industrial-agricultural, deliberately unremarkable.
physical_description.dimensions: Backpack body: 38 cm (H) × 28 cm (W) × 16 cm (D). Dispersal nozzle adds 12 cm forward projection. Fits within standard worker harness envelope.
physical_description.weight_description: 3.8 kg loaded (noticeable but balanced), worn across both shoulders via padded harness straps. Handheld canister swaps take ~90 seconds. Portable for sustained operational use.
physical_description.primary_material: Anodized aluminum pressure vessel housings, stainless steel valve manifold, food-grade polymer distribution tubing (beige/tan), rubber padding on shoulder contact points.
physical_description.finish: Matte industrial gray anodize on vessel caps, weathered brushed stainless on fittings. Tubing appears aged and utilitarian. No gloss surfaces — designed to photograph dull under surveillance.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray vessels, burnt-tan distribution tubing, brass valve accents, black pressure gauges with white numeric scales. Tan/khaki canvas harness with faded Ironclad Agrisystems stenciled logo (intentionally worn).
physical_description.interface_elements: Wrist-mounted brass dial controller (approximately 8 cm diameter) with 12-position rotary selector for dispersal rate (OFF, LO, MED, HI positions marked). Dual analog pressure gauges (one per vessel) with needle indicators. Quick-release canister coupling with red safety tabs. Manual purge valve on the nozzle assembly.
distinctive_features: Dual-canister configuration creates visible asymmetry — agricultural authenticity
Braided high-pressure hoses with vintage brass fittings (suggests legitimate horticultural pedigree)
Wrist dial separated from pack by 1.5 m of coiled tether — operator can adjust without reaching back
Faded Ironclad Agrisystems logo on canvas harness (faintly visible: 'Reflectance Optimization System - Model 7.2')
Nozzle flare designed to break up particle clouds into naturalistic dispersal patterns
Tiny vent holes in harness backing (cooling channels for extended use, appear incidental)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Embossed Ironclad Agrisystems logo on shoulder strap. Faded regulatory stamps on vessel caps (ISO compliance dates from 2219). Serial number plate on main manifold block (intentionally dull brass, difficult to read at distance).
physical_description.condition_typical: Used units show minor white residue deposits on nozzle edges (agricultural particulate buildup), slight valve stem discoloration (mineral residue), scratches on pressure gauges from field handling. Harness fabric shows sun fading consistent with rooftop agricultural work.
